seo-description: Deploy EVM smart contracts to the Sintrop impact blockchain with Hardhat, Foundry or Remix. Network config, a sample contract and step-by-step commands.
footerTagline: A public proof-of-work blockchain for social and environmental impact applications.
heroTitle: Deploy a contract with the tools you already use
heroLead: The Sintrop Virtual Machine is EVM-compatible. Write Solidity, point Hardhat, Foundry or Remix at the network, and ship an impact application without high gas fees.
why1Desc: SIN is a pure gas utility token with no pre-mine. Complex contracts stay affordable for the people who use them.
why2Desc: Same Solidity, same bytecode, same wallets. Your existing toolchain works by adding one network entry.
why3Desc: The ecosystem is built around social and environmental applications — not speculation.
why4Desc: Avoid privileged owner functions where you can. When setup requires them, call renounceOwnership afterwards.
connectLead: The same values for every tool and wallet.
guideLead: A minimal impact registry. Pick your tool and follow the steps.
sampleDesc: Save this as ImpactRegistry.sol. Anyone can publish a claim; the full list stays readable on-chain.
hardhatStep1Desc: Add a sintrop entry to your Hardhat config. Keep the deployer key in an environment variable, never in the file.
hardhatStep2Desc: Run your deploy script against the network. Hardhat prints the deployed address.
foundryStep1Desc: Register the network in foundry.toml so you can refer to it by name.
foundryStep2Desc: Use forge create with the Sintrop RPC and your deployer key from the environment.
remixStep1Desc: In your wallet, add a custom network with the RPC URL and chain ID above. Fund the account with a little SIN for gas.
remixStep2Desc: In Remix, compile the contract, then in the Deploy tab choose the "Injected Provider" environment so it uses your wallet on Sintrop. Confirm the transaction.
remixStep3Desc: Choose the "Custom - External Http Provider" environment and enter the RPC URL directly.
after1: Open the transaction on the explorer to confirm the contract address and code.
after2: Interact from a script, a frontend, or the explorer's read/write tabs.
after3: If your contract is Ownable and setup is done, send renounceOwnership() to keep it trustless.
